name: Mara Massey
life: “I still remember trying to sleep beside a fountain that ran all night.” Monday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Mara notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I can't stand the sound of running water at night. The student gave me the part that stops it.
appearance: Mara is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Mara starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Mara carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To give the piece a real ending.
family: Isaac Nord is Mara’s younger relative by marriage. Mara makes room at the table. Isaac brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The release address*, Isaac says, “I was the child writing envelopes for my mother.”
connections: Damian Harris. Breaking a pitched glass gives the player who hates running water a way to write silence into it.

reactions.situation: An instrument breaks before the fountain piece begins
reactions.response: Mara asks the player whether a different everyday object can carry the missing note.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Mara offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Mara offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
